newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parliament adopts pesticide residues reports.
newsitem.headline: Parliament adopts pesticide residues reports.

text.p: The European Parliament adopted its report on pesticide residues in various foods on Wednesday, heavily amending the European Commission's proposal in the process.

In adopting the report by German Green MEP Hiltrud Breyer, the Parliament completed its work under the consultation procedure on Commission proposal COM(95)272 for a Council directive to amend four directives on pesticide residues in or on food.
The four directives cover residues in or on fruit, vegetables, cereals, animal-origin foodstuffs and products of plant origin.
Euro-MPs adopted amendments 1 to 9, 12, 13, 15 to 21, 23 to 30, 32, 33 and 38 to 41. They rejected the remainder of the 51 amendments up for a vote.

The European Commission representatives indicated during Tuesday's debate that it would not be possible to change the proposal's legal base to bring it under Article 100A, as opposed to the present Article 43, as Breyer had sought.
